Meeting No. 28 and 29
Federal
Nepal
Parliament
Notice Paper - 2
(Brief Minutes of the Meeting Proceedings)
Sunday, Ashad 14, 2083
The first meeting of the House of Representatives today commenced at 11:05 AM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal.
At the beginning of the meeting, when Honourable Members from Nepali Congress, CPN (UML), Nepali Communist Party, and Shram Sanskriti Party stood up in front of their seats seeking time to speak, the Right Honourable Speaker granted time to the following Honourable Members, who expressed dissatisfaction that the Right Honourable Prime Minister, instead of responding in Parliament, was giving reactions based on the importance of the party's general convention.
"The Prime Minister's every statement should be considered an official political message of Nepal, and care must be taken to maintain the dignity of the office and diplomatic courtesy. The statement made by the Right Honourable Prime Minister on Jestha 17, stating that Nepal has encroached upon India's land, should be removed from the parliamentary records. The Vice-Chairman of CPN (UML), Bishnu Prasad Paudel, has been arrested based on political vendetta and charged with money laundering; he must be immediately released. It is alleged that the document passed by the Raswapa's general convention seeks to weaken the foundations of democracy and republicanism. Some ideologies that have emerged under the guise of popularity will push the country back into conflict. Promising to empower provincial and local levels while seeking votes and then adopting a policy to abolish those very structures after winning is a betrayal of the people. Was the statement made by Prime Minister Balendra Shah regarding the border in the national interest or against it? Raising this question, it was demanded that if the statement is in the national interest, it should not be removed from the record, and if it is against the national interest, it should be immediately removed. FIFA's suspension of ANFA is affecting the future of players, so the government must immediately take steps to lift the suspension."
Among other issues, they expressed their views.

Subsequently, during the impromptu session that began, the following Honourable Members expressed their views:
Regarding the tragic demise of 10-year-old girl Anukriti Chapagain at the bridge of Adhuba Khola in Birtabazar, Birtamod Municipality-3, Jhapa, heartfelt tribute and deep condolences were expressed to the bereaved family, and immediate action was demanded against the gang that threatened the victim's family and protected the perpetrator. The government must immediately take steps to lift FIFA's suspension of ANFA. The access road to the Arun-3 Hydropower Project in Sankhuwasabha has deteriorated due to rain and traffic, so the road needs to be upgraded. Just as citizens pay fines for violating traffic rules, the state should also make a law requiring compensation and fines to citizens for its shortcomings. Furthermore, action should be taken against the concerned bodies and construction entrepreneurs for accidents caused by the poor condition of the road. The potholes on the sides of the Butwal-Gorusinge road section of the East-West Highway are affecting daily life, so the concerned bodies should pay attention to the construction of this road. There is a shortage of anti-snake venom and anti-rabies vaccine in hospitals and health institutions in Kapilvastu, so these vaccines must be provided. The construction of roads including the BP Highway and the road from Ilam to Taplejung must be repaired and maintained as per the agreement as soon as possible. Although the Government of Nepal has approved the operation of Lamkichuha Hospital in Kailali as a provincial hospital for a long time, it has not been able to operate due to internal reasons of the municipality and the province, so immediate steps should be taken for its operation. The government has ordered the eviction of the hold center where the landless are housed, so an alternative arrangement must be made. Narayan Prasad Parajuli of Thulung Dudhkoshi, Solukhumbu, was seriously injured by an electric shock, so free treatment and compensation must be arranged. The National Examination Board hastily published the results of Grade 12, causing hardship to thousands of students and parents, so an impartial investigation into the errors in the results must be conducted and the guilty punished.
Among other issues, they expressed their views.

Thereafter, on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, the Honourable Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, presented the "Thirty-first Annual Report of the Auditor General, 2083".
Subsequently, on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, the Honourable Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, proposed to seek permission to present the "Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083".
Thereafter, as no notice of objection from any Honourable Member was received regarding the motion to seek permission to present the said bill, in accordance with Rule 105 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, the Honourable Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, presented the "Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083".

Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker informed about a minor adjustment in the agenda for today.
Thereafter, the Honourable Minister for Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation, Pratibha Rawal, proposed to seek permission to present the "Cooperatives (First Amendment) Bill, 2083".
Subsequently, as no notice of objection from any Honourable Member was received regarding the motion to seek permission to present the said bill, in accordance with Rule 105 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, the Honourable Minister for Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation, Pratibha Rawal, presented the "Cooperatives (First Amendment) Bill, 2083".
Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Health and Population, Nisha Mehta, proposed to seek permission to present the "Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts Related to Health Science Institutions, 2083".
Thereafter, as no notice of objection from any Honourable Member was received regarding the motion to seek permission to present the said bill, in accordance with Rule 105 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, the Honourable Minister for Health and Population, Nisha Mehta, presented the "Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts Related to Health Science Institutions, 2083".
Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, proposed to seek permission to present the "Money Laundering Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083".
Subsequently, as no notice of objection from any Honourable Member was received regarding the motion to seek permission to present the said bill, in accordance with Rule 105 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, presented the "Money Laundering Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083".
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker informed that the discussion on the "Financial Bill, 2083" was scheduled to commence on Ashad 11, 2083, after the management work began, but since the meeting could not be held on that day, the discussion would take place in today's meeting. It was also informed that 7 amendment notices had been received regarding the said bill. Furthermore, it was informed to the Honourable Members that during the discussion on the "Financial Bill, 2083", in accordance with Rule 152, Sub-rule (4) of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, discussions could only be held on administrative matters within the accountability of the Government of Nepal, local issues, or matters related to the monetary and economic policy of the Government of Nepal.

Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the said bill and informed that the Government of Nepal had accepted the following amendments to be included in the bill:-
"In Clause 34,
Add the words "or fine" after the word "arrears" wherever it appears.
Replace the words "incurred" with the words "determined".
In Sub-clause (1) of Clause 49,
Replace the words "applicable fine" in the clause title with the words "applicable fine, additional duty".
Replace the words "fine, interest" in Sub-clauses (1) and (2) with the words "fine, interest, additional duty".
Replace Sub-clause (25) of Clause 57 with the following Sub-clause (24):
(24) Replace Sub-clause (1) of Clause 119A with the following Sub-clause (1):
(1) In accordance with Sub-clause (4) of Clause 89, the taxpayer shall be charged a fee of five hundred thousand rupees for using software to modify or correct data for issuing electricity bills, and a fee of one hundred thousand rupees for failing to comply with other provisions of the same clause."
Subsequently, the Honourable Member Hari Prasad Bhusal withdrew his amendment, the Honourable Sushil Khadka withdrew amendments except those accepted by the Honourable Minister for Finance, and as the Honourable Speaker granted time for the Honourable Members who presented amendments to withdraw them, and they did not wish to withdraw, the amendment proposals were presented for decision and were rejected by a majority:-

Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker presented the amendments accepted by the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, in response to the "Financial Bill, 2083" for decision, and they were approved by a majority to become part of the "Financial Bill, 2083".
Subsequently, Clauses 2 to 61 of the bill and Schedules 1 to 11 related thereto were presented for decision to become part of the bill, and were approved by a majority.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker read out the preamble and title of the bill and presented them for decision to become part of the "Financial Bill, 2083", and they were approved by a majority.
Subsequently, the motion moved by the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, "Let the "Financial Bill, 2083" be passed" was presented for decision by the Right Honourable Speaker and was passed by a majority.

Subsequently, the motion moved by the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, "Let the clause-by-clause discussion on the "National Debt Raising Bill, 2083" be held in the House" was presented for decision by the Right Honourable Speaker and was approved by a majority.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker informed that the clause-by-clause discussion on the "National Debt Raising Bill, 2083" has commenced and that 3 amendment notices have been received regarding the said bill.
Subsequently, the following Honourable Members participated in the discussion by presenting their amendments: Honourable Hari Prasad Bhusal and Honourable Parshuram Tamang.

Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker read out the preamble and title of the bill and declared that they were unanimously approved to become part of the bill.
Subsequently, the motion moved by the Honourable Minister for Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, "Let the "National Debt Raising Bill, 2083" be passed" was presented for decision by the Right Honourable Speaker and was unanimously passed.
Thereafter, the meeting was adjourned until 2:35 PM today, with the next meeting of the House of Representatives to be held 15 minutes later.

Subsequently, Honourable Bishwaraj Pokharel sought impromptu time and stated that on Ashad 6, 2083, floods in Khani Khola and Badge Khola in Chisapani, Okhaldhunga district, had damaged more than 270 ropanis of land belonging to 86 families, two houses, three sheds, and six livestock, and a small bridge connecting various wards was also damaged, disrupting movement. Therefore, the government must provide appropriate relief and compensation as soon as possible.
Subsequently, the motion "Consider the "Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts Related to Health Science Institutions, 2083"" was presented for decision by the Right Honourable Speaker and was approved by a majority. Furthermore, it was informed that Honourable Members wishing to submit amendments to the "Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts Related to Health Science Institutions, 2083" in accordance with Rule 112 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, could register them at the Bill Section (House of Representatives), Federal Parliament Secretariat, Singhdarbar.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker presented a condolence motion on the demise of a former member of the House of Representatives, which was unanimously passed:-
Condolence Motion
"The House of Representatives expresses sorrow on the untimely demise of Rajendra Kharel, who was elected as a Member of Parliament from Kavrepalanchok District Election Constituency No. 4 in the general election of 2046 BS, played a leading role in the democratic system, served as the former State Minister of Education and the former Minister for Women, Children and Social Welfare, at the age of 80 on Jestha 7, 2083, during treatment, and offers condolences to the bereaved family."
Subsequently, the House stood for one minute of silence in memory of the late Rajendra Kharel.
Thereafter, the House of Representatives was adjourned until Thursday, Ashad 18, 2083, at 11:00 AM, at 5:45 PM today.
